items.plain: David praises God for sending Abigail, and thanks her for her good sense, which stopped him that day from shedding blood and taking revenge himself.
items.core_idea: Good counsel can stop us from taking revenge.

items.plain: Saul admits he has done wrong. Because David spared his life, he promises to stop harming him and confesses he has acted like a fool and gone badly astray.
items.core_idea: Being spared can bring an honest admission of wrong.

items.plain: David was in deep trouble: his grieving people, who had lost their children, talked of stoning him. Yet he found strength in the Lord his God.
items.core_idea: In crisis, strength can be drawn from God.

items.plain: Those who stay behind to guard the supplies get the same share as those who go into battle. Everyone shares equally.
items.core_idea: Those who support the work share equally in reward.

items.plain: Paul wants believers to understand what happens to those who have died, so they do not grieve without hope: as Jesus died and rose, God will bring the dead in Jesus with him.
items.core_idea: Grief need not be hopeless for those in Jesus.

items.plain: Paul urges correcting the unruly, encouraging the timid, helping the weak and being patient with everyone. Never repay wrong with wrong; always seek good. Rejoice always, pray constantly, and give thanks in everything, as God wills.
items.core_idea: Be patient, do good, rejoice, pray and give thanks.

items.plain: It is true and worth accepting that Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and Paul counts himself the worst. He was shown mercy so Jesus could display his patience in him as an example for future believers.
items.core_idea: Even the worst sinner can receive mercy.

items.plain: Do not let anyone look down on you for being young. Instead, set an example for believers in how you speak, live, love, and in your spirit, faith and purity.
items.core_idea: Being young is no bar to setting an example.

items.plain: Living for God with contentment is real wealth. We bring nothing into the world and take nothing out, so food and clothing are enough. Chasing riches leads to ruin; loving money is a root of every kind of evil.
items.core_idea: Contentment is wealth; love of money brings ruin.

items.plain: Tell the rich not to be proud or trust uncertain wealth, but to trust the living God who gives everything to enjoy. They should do good, be generous and share, building a foundation for eternal life.
items.core_idea: The rich should trust God and be generous.

items.plain: God tells Solomon to ask for anything. Solomon thanks God for his kindness to David and, feeling the weight of ruling a vast people, asks only for wisdom and knowledge to lead them.
items.core_idea: Asked for anything, Solomon asks for wisdom.

items.plain: David wanted to build a temple for God. God told him it was good that he wanted to, but that his son, not he, would build it.
items.core_idea: A good intention matters even if another fulfils it.

items.plain: God says that when he brings drought, locusts or plague, if his people humble themselves, pray, seek him and turn from their wrongdoing, he will hear them, forgive them and heal their land.
items.core_idea: Humility and turning from wrong bring God's healing.

items.plain: King Rehoboam asked his father's old advisers what to do; they said that if he was kind to the people, they would serve him forever. But he rejected their advice and turned to the young men he grew up with.
items.core_idea: Rejecting wise elders' counsel for peers' approval.

items.plain: A prayer to the Lord: only you can help the weak against the strong. Help us, for we rely on you and face this huge army in your name. Do not let mere people win against you.
items.core_idea: The weak rely on God against overwhelming odds.

items.plain: Be strong and do not let your hands go limp, because your work will be rewarded.
items.core_idea: Keep going; your work will be rewarded.

items.plain: I swear by the living Lord: I will say whatever my God tells me to say.
items.core_idea: Speak only what God says, whatever the pressure.

items.plain: We do not know what to do, but we are looking to you.
items.core_idea: When lost, look to God.

items.plain: Do not be afraid or discouraged by this huge army, because the fight is not yours; it is God's.
items.core_idea: The battle belongs to God, not you.

items.plain: Amaziah worries about the large sum he already paid to hire an army. The man of God replies that the Lord can give him far more than that.
items.core_idea: God can give far more than what you lose.

items.plain: A prayer that the good Lord will forgive everyone who sincerely seeks God, even if they have not met the temple's purity rules.
items.core_idea: A heart seeking God matters more than ritual purity.

items.plain: Be strong and brave; do not fear the king of Assyria and his huge army. One greater is with us: he has only human strength, but the Lord our God is with us to help and fight for us.
items.core_idea: God with us outweighs any human power.

items.plain: Praise to God, the Father of mercies and source of all comfort, who comforts us in every trouble so that we can comfort others in theirs with the comfort God gave us.
items.core_idea: Comfort received from God is meant to be passed on.

items.plain: Our treasure is held in fragile clay jars, so the great power is shown to be God's, not ours. Pressed, confused, hunted and knocked down, we are never crushed, despairing, abandoned or destroyed, so Jesus' life shows in us.
items.core_idea: Fragile people, sustained by God's power, are not crushed.

items.plain: So we do not lose heart. Our bodies wear out, but inside we are renewed daily. Brief troubles produce lasting glory, as we look not at what is seen, which passes, but at what is unseen, which is eternal.
items.core_idea: Outer decay, inner renewal; the unseen is eternal.

items.plain: Anyone who is in Christ is made new. The old has gone; everything has become new.
items.core_idea: In Christ, a person is made entirely new.

items.plain: Sorrow that comes from God leads to a change of heart and to salvation, with nothing to regret. But the world's kind of sorrow leads to death.
items.core_idea: Godly sorrow heals; worldly sorrow kills.

items.plain: If you are willing, your gift is welcome for what you have, not judged by what you do not have.
items.core_idea: Willingness counts; give from what you have.

items.plain: Whoever sows little reaps little; whoever sows generously reaps generously. Each should give what they have decided in their heart, not reluctantly or under pressure, because God loves a cheerful giver.
items.core_idea: Give generously and gladly; God loves a cheerful giver.

items.plain: Paul will not class or compare himself with those who praise themselves. People who measure themselves against themselves and compare themselves with each other show they lack understanding.
items.core_idea: Measuring yourself by yourself shows a lack of understanding.

items.plain: The Lord told Paul his grace is enough, because his power is made complete in weakness. So Paul gladly boasts of and takes pleasure in his weaknesses and hardships for Christ, because when he is weak, he is strong.
items.core_idea: God's power shows most in our weakness.

items.plain: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Grow toward maturity, be comforted, agree with one another, live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
items.core_idea: Live in peace; the God of peace is with you.

items.plain: The Lord says: you have not really abandoned me; you have abandoned yourselves.
items.core_idea: Turning from God is abandoning yourself.

fix.display_text: You have not as it were forsaken me, but your own selves, says the Lord.

items.plain: God commands: treat widows rightly, defend the fatherless and orphans, give to the poor, clothe the naked, heal the broken and weak, never mock the lame, protect the maimed, help the blind, and look after old and young.
items.core_idea: Care for the vulnerable is God's command.

items.plain: Be still, my people, and rest, because your peace is coming.
items.core_idea: Rest; peace is coming.

items.plain: Do not worry too much. When the time of trouble and anguish comes, others will weep and grieve, but you will be glad and have plenty.
items.core_idea: Do not overworry; God's people will be cared for.

items.plain: The angel answers that you cannot hurry ahead of the Most High: your haste is for yourself alone, but God's timing serves many.
items.core_idea: God's timing serves many; our haste serves ourselves.

items.plain: I know what has already happened, but I do not know what is still to come.
items.core_idea: The past is known; the future is not.

items.plain: Waking from a vision, he shook all over and his mind was so troubled it gave way. The angel held him, comforted him and helped him back onto his feet.
items.core_idea: In terror, comfort lifts us back to our feet.

items.plain: He asks the Lord why he was born at all, and why he did not die at birth, so he would not have to see the suffering and weary toil of Israel's people.
items.core_idea: Despair asks why one was born to see suffering.

items.plain: On the eighth night his heart was troubled again and he began to speak before the Most High, his spirit burning and his soul in distress.
items.core_idea: A troubled soul pours itself out before God.

items.plain: The angel compares it to a vast sea whose only entrance is narrow like a river: whoever wants to reach the open sea must first pass through the narrow way.
items.core_idea: The broad place is reached only through the narrow.

items.plain: Why are you so troubled, when you are only a mortal who will perish? Why have you not thought about what is to come rather than only about what is happening now?
items.core_idea: Mortals should look to what comes, not only now.

items.plain: He asks the earth why it brought forth a mind from dust. It would be better if the dust had never been, because the mind grows with us, and so we suffer: we die and we know it.
items.core_idea: Knowing we will die torments the human mind.

items.plain: He tells his soul to take in understanding and his heart to feed on wisdom, because we arrive without choosing it, leave when we do not wish to, and are given only a short time to live.
items.core_idea: Life is short; seek understanding while you can.

items.plain: He asks God why he should be so angry with frail, mortal humans, since truly no one ever born has not done wrong and fallen short.
items.core_idea: Every human does wrong; God, why such anger?

items.plain: So keep your grief to yourself, and face the misfortunes that have come to you with courage.
items.core_idea: Bear misfortune with courage.

items.plain: Shake off your heavy grief and set aside your many sorrows, so that the Mighty One may show you mercy again and the Most High may give you rest from your troubles.
items.core_idea: Letting go of sorrow opens the way to God's rest.

items.plain: I am still weary in mind and very weak in spirit; I have no strength left at all because of the great terror I felt tonight.
items.core_idea: Fear can leave us utterly drained.

items.plain: Take comfort, Israel, and do not grieve, people of Jacob: the Most High remembers you, and the Mighty One has not forgotten you forever.
items.core_idea: God has not forgotten his people.

items.plain: You have ordered your life by wisdom, and have treated understanding as your mother.
items.core_idea: A life guided by wisdom and understanding.

items.plain: The world has lost its youth, and the ages are starting to grow old.
items.core_idea: The world itself is growing old.

items.plain: Do not be afraid of what they plot against you, and do not let the disbelief of those who speak against you upset you.
items.core_idea: Do not let critics' disbelief trouble you.

items.plain: The Lord God says: do not be afraid or doubt, for God guides you. You who keep my commands, do not let your sins weigh you down or your wrongdoings rise up over you.
items.core_idea: Do not fear; God guides; sins need not crush you.

fix.display_text: Be you not afraid, neither doubt; for God is your guide: and you who keep my commandments and precepts, says the Lord God, don’t let your sins weigh you down, and don’t let your iniquities lift up themselves.

items.plain: I have much to write to you, but I would rather not use paper and ink. I hope to visit and talk face to face, so our joy can be complete.
items.core_idea: Joy is fullest face to face.

items.plain: Elijah asks Elisha to stay behind, as the Lord has sent him on to Bethel. Elisha swears by the Lord and by Elijah's life that he will not leave him, so they go on together.
items.core_idea: Loyal companionship refuses to leave.

items.plain: Naaman storms off, angry the prophet only told him to wash in the Jordan instead of healing him with ceremony. His servants reason that he would have done something great if asked, so why not something simple?
items.core_idea: Pride can make us refuse simple remedies.

items.plain: Seeing an army surrounding the city, Elisha's servant panics. Elisha tells him not to fear, since more are with them than against them, and prays; the Lord opens the servant's eyes to hills full of fiery horses and chariots.
items.core_idea: Unseen help is greater than the visible threat.

items.plain: Four men with leprosy at the city gate reason that staying put or entering the starving city both mean death. So they decide to go to the enemy camp: if spared they live, and if killed they only die.
items.core_idea: When every option risks death, take the one with hope.

items.plain: King Jehoash warns Amaziah with a fable of a thistle that asked a cedar for a marriage and was trampled by a beast. Proud of beating Edom, Amaziah should enjoy his glory at home rather than invite ruin.
items.core_idea: Pride after success invites a fall.

items.plain: Hezekiah is dying, and Isaiah brings word from the Lord to put his affairs in order. Hezekiah turns to the wall and prays, asking the Lord to remember his faithful, wholehearted life, and weeps bitterly.
items.core_idea: Facing death, a faithful man weeps and prays.

items.plain: A mother tells her sons that she does not know how they came to be in her womb; she did not give them breath and life, nor shape the parts of their bodies.
items.core_idea: Life comes from beyond the parents who bear it.

fix.display_text: I know not how you came into my womb, neither was it I that bestowed on you your spirit and your life, and it was not I that brought into order the first elements of each one of you.

items.plain: The mother begs her son to look at the heavens and the earth and all that is in them, and see that God made them out of nothing, and that people come into being the same way.
items.core_idea: God made everything, and us, from nothing.

items.plain: If I have told my story well and to the point, that is what I wanted; if it is poor and ordinary, it is the best I could do.
items.core_idea: Offering one's best, whether good or ordinary.

items.plain: Do not forget that to the Lord a day is like a thousand years and a thousand years like a day. He is not slow to keep his promise, but patient, wanting no one to perish and everyone to repent.
items.core_idea: God's delay is patience, not slowness.

items.plain: David laments: how the mighty have fallen in battle! He grieves for his brother Jonathan, who was dear to him, whose love for him was wonderful, greater than the love of women.
items.core_idea: Grief for a beloved friend fallen in battle.

items.plain: Abner calls to Joab: must the killing go on forever? Don't you know it will end in bitterness? How long before you call your people back from chasing their own brothers?
items.core_idea: Endless fighting between brothers ends in bitterness.

items.plain: King David sits before the Lord and asks who he is, and what his family is, that God has brought him this far.
items.core_idea: Humble wonder at how far God has brought us.

items.plain: Be brave, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God, and may the Lord do what he thinks best.
items.core_idea: Do your part bravely; leave the outcome to God.

items.plain: The Lord sends Nathan to David with a story: a rich man with huge flocks, wanting to feed a guest, took instead a poor man's only lamb, which he had raised like a daughter, and served it.
items.core_idea: The powerful taking the little the poor have.

items.plain: David fasted and wept while his child lived, hoping the Lord might spare him. Once the child died, he ate. He cannot bring the child back; David will go to him, but the child will not return.
items.core_idea: Hope while there is hope; then accept death.

items.plain: We must all die, like water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered again. Yet God does not take life away, but finds ways so that the banished one is not cut off from him.
items.core_idea: We are mortal, but God makes ways back for outcasts.

items.plain: Ittai swears by the Lord and by the king's life that wherever the king goes, in life or death, he will be there too.
items.core_idea: Loyalty that follows in life or death.

items.plain: Fleeing, King David sends God's ark back to the city. If the Lord favours him, he will bring him back to see it; if not, David says, here I am, let God do with me what he thinks good.
items.core_idea: Surrendering one's fate to God's will.

items.plain: Deeply shaken, the king goes up to the room over the gate and weeps, crying out for his son Absalom and wishing he had died in his place.
items.core_idea: A father's grief, wishing to have died instead.

items.plain: Old Barzillai tells the king he is eighty and has few years left: he can no longer tell good from bad, taste food or drink, or hear singers. Why should he go to Jerusalem and be a burden?
items.core_idea: In old age, not wanting to be a burden.

items.plain: Please let me go back home so I can die in my own town, near the grave of my father and mother.
items.core_idea: Wishing to die at home, near one's parents.

items.plain: Death and evil surrounded me like waves and floods, and its snares caught me. In my distress I called to the Lord, my God, and he heard my voice and my cry from his temple.
items.core_idea: In overwhelming distress, God hears our cry.

items.plain: Lord, you are my lamp; the Lord will light up my darkness.
items.core_idea: God lights up our darkness.

items.plain: God, the Rock of Israel, said that one who rules people justly and in awe of God is like morning light at sunrise on a cloudless day, like grass sprouting in the clear shine after rain.
items.core_idea: Just rule in awe of God is like morning light.

items.plain: After taking a census, David's conscience strikes him. He tells the Lord he has sinned greatly and acted very foolishly, and begs him to take away his guilt.
items.core_idea: A troubled conscience confesses and asks forgiveness.

items.plain: The king refuses Araunah's gift and insists on paying, saying he will not offer the Lord his God sacrifices that cost him nothing.
items.core_idea: A true offering must cost you something.

items.plain: But you, brothers, do not grow tired of doing what is right.
items.core_idea: Do not tire of doing right.

items.plain: May the Lord of peace himself give you peace always and in every way. The Lord be with you all.
items.core_idea: May the Lord give you peace always.

items.plain: God did not give us a spirit of fear, but one of power, love and self-control.
items.core_idea: God gives power, love and self-control, not fear.

items.plain: My life is already being poured out, and the time for me to depart has come. I have fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith.
items.core_idea: Facing death having lived faithfully to the end.

items.plain: At my first trial everyone deserted me; may it not be held against them. But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so the message could be fully preached, and I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
items.core_idea: Deserted by all, but the Lord stood by me.

items.plain: Dear friend, I pray that all goes well with you and that you are healthy, just as your soul is doing well.
items.core_idea: Wishing body and life to thrive as the soul does.

items.plain: Dear friend, do not copy what is evil, but what is good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God.
items.core_idea: Imitate good; doing good shows you are of God.

items.plain: A prayer asking God to wipe out our sins and mistakes, to show compassion now, to send mercy quickly ahead of us, and to grant peace so that the downcast and broken-hearted may praise him.
items.core_idea: Plea for mercy and peace for the broken-hearted.

items.plain: A prayer recalling that when Jonah was wasting away inside the sea monster, God the Father watched over him and brought him back to his own people.
items.core_idea: God sees and rescues even from the depths.

items.plain: You may not be able to remove anger or malice from your soul, but you can resist them. Reason does not wipe out the passions; it stands against them and helps you not give in.
items.core_idea: Reason cannot erase passions, but can resist them.

items.plain: Desire comes before pleasure, and joy after it. Fear comes before pain, and sorrow after it.
items.core_idea: Pleasure and pain each have feelings before and after.

items.plain: Only the wise and brave person is master of their passions.
items.core_idea: Only the wise and brave master their passions.

items.plain: Birds on our rooftops defend their chicks; others nest on mountaintops, cliffs and trees and drive off intruders. If they cannot, they circle overhead crying out in anguished love, saving their young however they can.
items.core_idea: Even birds fight with love to protect their young.

items.plain: All the believers lived together and shared everything, selling their property to give to anyone in need. Every day they met in the temple, ate together at home with glad, sincere hearts, praised God, and were liked by everyone.
items.core_idea: Early believers shared everything with glad hearts.

items.plain: If this plan or movement is merely human, it will fail. But if it comes from God, you will not be able to stop it, and you may even find yourselves fighting against God.
items.core_idea: What is from God cannot be overthrown.

items.plain: I now truly see that God has no favourites; in every nation, anyone who reveres him and does what is right is accepted by him.
items.core_idea: God accepts the upright of every nation.

items.plain: God, who made the world, does not live in temples or need anything; he gives all life and breath. He made every nation to seek and find him, though he is near each of us, for in him we live.
items.core_idea: God is near us; in him we live and move.

items.plain: Paul says the Spirit compels him to Jerusalem; he knows only that prison and hardship await. He does not value his life, if only he can joyfully finish his race and the work Jesus gave him.
items.core_idea: Finishing one's calling matters more than one's life.

items.plain: Paul says his life showed them that, by working hard, we should help the weak and remember Jesus' words: giving brings more blessing than receiving.
items.core_idea: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

items.plain: Can two people walk together unless they have agreed to?
items.core_idea: Walking together requires agreement.

items.plain: Seek good and not evil so that you may live, and then the Lord, the God of Armies, will truly be with you, as you claim. Hate evil, love good, and make sure there is justice in the courts.
items.core_idea: Seek good, hate evil, establish justice.

items.plain: Let justice flow like rivers, and right living like a mighty stream that never stops.
items.core_idea: Let justice flow like a river.

items.plain: The Lord says a time is coming when he will send a famine, not of food or water, but of hearing his words. People will wander everywhere searching for the Lord's word and will not find it.
items.core_idea: A famine of hearing God's word.

items.plain: Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a soul in anguish and a troubled spirit cries out to you.
items.core_idea: A soul in anguish cries out to God.

items.plain: Learn where wisdom, strength and understanding are found, so you also know where to find long life, the light of the eyes, and peace.
items.core_idea: Seek wisdom, and with it life and peace.

items.plain: Where are the rulers of nations, those who mastered beasts and birds, those who hoarded endless silver and gold that people trust in, and the skilled craftsmen? They have vanished into the grave, and others have taken their place.
items.core_idea: The powerful and rich all pass into the grave.

items.plain: Jerusalem, as a mother, tells her children to go on their way, since she is left desolate. She has taken off the clothes of peace and put on sackcloth, and will cry to the Everlasting as long as she lives.
items.core_idea: In desolation, crying to God for life.

items.plain: Fix your thoughts on the things above, not on earthly things.
items.core_idea: Set your mind on things above.

items.plain: As God's chosen, loved people, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility and patience. Bear with and forgive one another as Christ forgave you. Above all, love, which binds everything together; let God's peace rule your hearts; be thankful.
items.core_idea: Clothe yourself in compassion, forgiveness and love.

items.plain: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they do not lose heart.
items.core_idea: Don't provoke your children into discouragement.

items.plain: Whatever you do, put your whole heart into it, as working for the Lord rather than for people, knowing the Lord will reward you, since it is Christ you serve.
items.core_idea: Work wholeheartedly, as for the Lord.

items.plain: Act wisely toward outsiders, making the most of your time. Let your speech always be gracious and flavoured with salt, so you know how to answer each person.
items.core_idea: Speak with grace and use time wisely.

items.plain: Daniel praises God forever, for wisdom and power are his. He changes times and seasons, removes and sets up kings, gives wisdom to the wise, reveals deep secrets, and knows what lies in darkness, for light lives with him.
items.core_idea: God holds wisdom, power and the course of history.

items.plain: Three young men tell King Nebuchadnezzar their God can save them from the blazing furnace and will rescue them. But even if he does not, they will never serve the king's gods or worship his golden statue.
items.core_idea: Faithful even if God does not rescue.

items.plain: A figure like a man touched Daniel again and strengthened him, saying: greatly loved one, do not fear; peace be with you; be strong, be strong. As he spoke, Daniel was strengthened and told him to speak.
items.core_idea: Be strong, you are loved; peace be with you.

items.plain: The wise will shine like the bright sky, and those who lead many to do right will shine like the stars forever.
items.core_idea: The wise and those who lead others rightly will shine.

items.plain: How can I carry all your problems, burdens and quarrels on my own?
items.core_idea: No one can carry everyone's burdens alone.

items.plain: Do not take sides when judging; hear the humble and the powerful the same. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgment belongs to God.
items.core_idea: Judge fairly and fear no one; judgment is God's.

items.plain: The Lord your God has blessed all your work and watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. For forty years he has been with you, and you have not lacked anything.
items.core_idea: God was with you through the wilderness; you lacked nothing.

items.plain: Listen, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord alone. Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul and all your strength.
items.core_idea: Love the one God with everything you have.

items.plain: Remember how the Lord led you forty years in the wilderness to humble and test you. He let you hunger, then fed you manna, to teach that people live not by bread alone but by every word from the Lord.
items.core_idea: People live not by bread alone but by God's word.

items.plain: Take it to heart that the Lord your God disciplines you just as a parent disciplines a child.
items.core_idea: God disciplines us as a parent does a child.

items.plain: Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you? Only to revere him, follow all his ways, love him, serve him with all your heart and soul, and keep his commands, which are for your own good.
items.core_idea: God asks for reverence, love and wholehearted service.

items.plain: The Lord your God is the great, mighty, awesome God of gods. He takes no bribes and plays no favourites; he defends orphans and widows and loves foreigners, feeding and clothing them. So love foreigners; you were foreigners in Egypt.
items.core_idea: Love the foreigner, as God does; you were one too.

items.plain: If any of your fellow people in your land is poor, do not harden your heart or close your hand to them. Open your hand freely and lend them enough for whatever they need.
items.core_idea: Don't harden your heart; open your hand to the poor.

items.plain: Give freely and without resentment, and the Lord your God will bless all your work. There will always be poor people in the land, so I command you to be open-handed toward the needy and poor among you.
items.core_idea: Give freely and gladly to the poor.

items.plain: Do not twist justice or play favourites. Do not take bribes, because a bribe blinds the wise and corrupts the words of the righteous. Pursue justice and only justice, so you may live in the land God gives you.
items.core_idea: Pursue justice; bribes blind even the wise.

items.plain: When you go to war and face horses, chariots and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, is with you.
items.core_idea: Facing greater forces, do not fear; God is with you.

items.plain: If you see your neighbour's donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not look away. You must help him get it back on its feet.
items.core_idea: Don't look away; help your neighbour up.

items.plain: Be careful to do what you have said. Whatever you freely vowed to the Lord your God with your own mouth, you must carry out.
items.core_idea: Keep the promises you make.

items.plain: Do not exploit a poor hired worker, whether Israelite or foreigner. Pay them each day before sunset, since they are poor and counting on it; otherwise they may cry to the Lord against you, and you will be guilty.
items.core_idea: Pay the poor worker promptly and fairly.

items.plain: When you harvest and forget a bundle of grain in the field, do not go back for it. Leave it for foreigners, orphans and widows, so the Lord your God will bless all your work.
items.core_idea: Leave something for the poor and the stranger.

items.plain: Your life will hang in doubt; you will be afraid day and night, never sure you will live. In the morning you will wish for evening, and at evening for morning, because of the dread in your heart.
items.core_idea: Constant dread makes every hour unbearable.

items.plain: Hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but what has been revealed belongs to us and our children forever, so that we may live by all the words of this law.
items.core_idea: Leave the hidden to God; live by what is revealed.

items.plain: This command is not too hard or out of reach. It is not in heaven or across the sea for someone to fetch. The word is very near you, in your mouth and heart, so you can do it.
items.core_idea: God's word is near, in your mouth and heart.

items.plain: With heaven and earth as witnesses, Moses sets before the people life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, for you and your children, by loving the Lord, obeying him and clinging to him, for he is your life.
items.core_idea: Choose life by loving and holding to God.

items.plain: The Lord himself goes ahead of you and will be with you. He will never fail or abandon you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.
items.core_idea: God goes ahead and will never abandon you.

items.plain: The eternal God is your home, and his everlasting arms are underneath you.
items.core_idea: God's everlasting arms hold you up.

items.plain: Your strength will last as long as your days.
items.core_idea: You will have strength for each day.

items.plain: Everything is wearisome beyond words. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear of hearing. What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
items.core_idea: Nothing is new; desire is never satisfied.

items.plain: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is missing cannot be counted.
items.core_idea: Some things simply cannot be fixed.

items.plain: I set my mind to understand wisdom as well as madness and folly, and saw that this too was chasing the wind. For with much wisdom comes much grief; whoever increases knowledge increases sorrow.
items.core_idea: More knowledge brings more sorrow.

items.plain: I denied myself nothing my eyes wanted and no pleasure, and enjoyed my work as my reward. But when I looked at all I had done, it was all empty, chasing the wind, with no real gain under the sun.
items.core_idea: Getting everything you want still leaves you empty.

items.plain: Nothing is better for a person than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in their work. I saw that this too comes from God's hand.
items.core_idea: Enjoying simple things and work is God's gift.

items.plain: There is a right time for everything under heaven: to be born and to die, to plant and uproot, to weep and laugh, to mourn and dance, to be silent and speak, to love and hate, for war and peace.
items.core_idea: Everything in life has its season.

items.plain: One handful with peace and quiet is better than two handfuls with toil and chasing the wind.
items.core_idea: Less with peace beats more with toil.

items.plain: Someone alone, with no son or brother, works without end and is never satisfied with his wealth. He never asks who he is working for, depriving himself of enjoyment. This too is empty, a miserable business.
items.core_idea: Endless toil for no one is empty and miserable.

items.plain: Two are better than one; they gain more from their work. If one falls, the other lifts them up; pity the one who falls alone. Two keep warm and resist attackers; a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
items.core_idea: Companions lift, warm and defend each other.

items.plain: Whoever loves money never has enough, and whoever loves wealth is never satisfied; this too is empty. More goods bring more mouths to feed. A worker sleeps soundly, but the rich man's plenty keeps him awake.
items.core_idea: Love of wealth never satisfies and costs sleep.

items.plain: It is better to enjoy what is in front of your eyes than to let your desires roam. Yet this too is empty, a chasing of the wind.
items.core_idea: Enjoy what you have rather than craving more.

items.plain: Better to visit a house of mourning than a feast, since death is everyone's end and the living should take it to heart. Sorrow is better than laughter; it improves the heart. The wise think on mourning, fools on fun.
items.core_idea: Facing death and sorrow makes the heart wiser.

items.plain: The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience better than pride. Do not be quick to anger; anger lives in fools. Do not ask why the old days were better; that is not wise.
items.core_idea: Be patient, slow to anger, and don't idealise the past.

items.plain: When times are good, be glad; when times are bad, reflect. God has made both, side by side, so that no one can discover what lies ahead.
items.core_idea: Enjoy good days; reflect in bad ones; God made both.

items.plain: No one on earth is so righteous that they do only good and never sin. So do not listen to everything people say, or you may hear your servant curse you; you know you have often cursed others yourself.
items.core_idea: Everyone sins; don't take every word to heart.

items.plain: Eat and drink with joy, for God already approves what you do. Enjoy life with the wife you love through your fleeting days. Do everything with all your might; in the grave there is no work or wisdom.
items.core_idea: Enjoy life and work fully; the grave ends all.

items.plain: I saw that the race is not won by the fastest, nor the battle by the strongest; food does not always go to the wise, wealth to the clever, or favour to the skilled. Time and chance happen to everyone.
items.core_idea: Time and chance happen to everyone.

items.plain: If a ruler becomes angry with you, do not leave your post, because calmness can put great offences to rest.
items.core_idea: Calmness can settle great offences.

items.plain: Whoever waits for perfect weather will never sow or reap. You cannot know how the wind moves or a baby grows, nor God's work. So sow morning and evening; you do not know which will succeed, or whether both.
items.core_idea: Don't wait for certainty; act, since outcomes are unknown.
